note: Adapted from Maiti 2006; original in English; the text notes 'Measurements: Table 13 (S.)', but Table 13 actually covers amboinensis and beckeri, the measurements of this species are in Table 14 and were taken from Table 14.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One of the smallest species of the genus, closest to C. emersoni; it differs from the latter in the wider postmentum waist and the shorter mandibles. In the soldier the narrowest part of the head lies below the maximum width, the anterior margin is nearly straight and the posterior margin weakly concave; pronotum nearly kidney-shaped, its length slightly more than half its width, distinctly narrower than the head width. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown (yellow in the holotype), labrum yellowish brown; pronotum, abdomen and legs light brown tinged with yellow. Head sparsely hairy, pronotum with erect hairs. The narrowest part of the head lies below the maximum width, anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin weakly concave; pronotum nearly kidney-shaped, its length slightly more than half its width, distinctly narrower than the head width, anterior margin weakly convex with a median notch, sides broadly rounded, posterior margin nearly straight. Measurements (mm): head length to the lateral base of the mandible 1.05—1.08; maximum head width 0.90—0.93; anterior head width 0.50; head height 0.68—0.71; head index 0.85; mandible length 0.60; head—mandible index 0.56; postmentum midlength 0.60—0.67, maximum width 0.33, waist width 0.18—0.22; pronotum length 0.34—0.37, width 0.60—0.67; pronotum index 0.53; pronotum/head width index 0.69; antennae 13-segmented.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality: Bentong, Malaysia, known only from the type locality. The holotype is a soldier, the worker is a morphotype, in the same vial as the holotype, in F.R.I. Dehra Dun; paratype soldiers are deposited in F.R.I. Dehra Dun, the American Museum of Natural History and the Zoological Survey of India (Calcutta). As Maiti had no material to examine, the description and measurements follow Krishna (1956).
